categories.prompt: Name a stadium, arena or racetrack used for professional sports.

categories.prompt: Name a piece of equipment an athlete wears.

categories.prompt: Name a movie that is a sequel to another movie.

categories.prompt: Name an animated TV series.

categories.prompt: Name a sitcom.

categories.prompt: Name a movie or TV character with superpowers.
categories.scope: A named character must have a supernatural or superhuman ability in the story.

categories.prompt: Name an actor who appears in a Marvel Cinematic Universe movie.

categories.prompt: Name a villain from a children's animated TV series.

categories.prompt: Name a fictional city or town from a movie or TV show.

categories.prompt: Name a horror movie villain or monster.
categories.scope: Named villains, creatures and monster species from horror films count.

categories.prompt: Name a song with a person's name in its title.

categories.prompt: Name a musical artist or band with a number in their name.

categories.prompt: Name a music group with at least three members.

categories.prompt: Name a rapper, past or present.

categories.prompt: Name a music festival.

categories.prompt: Name a musician known professionally by one name.

categories.prompt: Name a musical instrument played by blowing air into it.

categories.prompt: Name something sold as a pizza topping.

categories.prompt: Name something people put inside a sandwich.

categories.prompt: Name a fast-food or fast-casual restaurant chain.

categories.prompt: Name a drink you can order at a coffee shop.

categories.prompt: Name a fruit used in a sweet dessert.

categories.prompt: Name an animal that can deliver venom.

categories.prompt: Name an animal that changes color.

categories.prompt: Name an animal that flies but is not a bird.

categories.prompt: Name a wild animal that spends time both in water and on land.
categories.scope: The animal must normally use both habitats, not merely survive a brief swim.

categories.prompt: Name a kind of shark or ray.

categories.prompt: Name an animal that lays eggs.

categories.prompt: Name an animal that is active at night.

categories.prompt: Name an animal people have used for work or transport.

categories.prompt: Name a plant people eat.

categories.prompt: Name a plant that has thorns, spines or prickles.

categories.prompt: Name a named object in our Solar System.

categories.prompt: Name something people use to measure things.

categories.prompt: Name a machine or device that uses an electric motor.

categories.prompt: Name something that produces visible light.

categories.prompt: Name a weather event or weather condition.

categories.prompt: Name a named pasta or noodle dish.
categories.scope: Named dishes and established menu preparations count, including familiar meal names such as spaghetti, udon and soba, filled pastas and gnocchi. categories.prompt: Name an item or product used to wash, dry or care for laundry.
categories.scope: Laundry appliances, supplies, stain treatments and clothes-care tools count, as do named product types and established laundry-product brands, including historical ones. A garment itself is not a laundry supply.

categories.prompt: Name an object that commonly has a hinge.
categories.scope: A common hinged version of the object must exist. Sliding or roll-up versions do not prevent a genuinely hinged object from counting.

categories.prompt: Name a hand tool or utensil used to prepare or serve food.
categories.scope: Kitchen hand tools, utensils, serving implements and nonpowered cookware count. Small measuring tools used in food preparation also count. Large powered appliances and foods do not qualify.

categories.prompt: Name a combat sport or established martial art.
categories.scope: Named competitive fighting disciplines and established martial arts count, including forms practiced without full-contact competition. Fictional styles do not count.

categories.prompt: Name a sport or recognized sporting discipline played on snow or ice.
categories.scope: Established ice and snow sports and competitive disciplines count. A sport merely played during the winter on an ordinary indoor court does not qualify.

categories.prompt: Name an exercise that can be done using your bodyweight instead of added weights.
categories.scope: Named exercises and recognized variations count, including floor exercises, holds and movements on a pull-up bar. A bar or bench can provide support; dumbbells and loaded barbells are not required.

categories.prompt: Name a player who has won the NBA regular-season MVP award.
categories.scope: Winners of the main NBA regular-season Most Valuable Player award through the 2025–26 season count. Finals, All-Star and other leagues' MVP awards are different.

categories.prompt: Name a real animal that has horns or antlers.
categories.scope: Living and extinct animals count, including beetle horns and other actual horn-like structures. Feathers that merely look like horns do not count. A named animal group counts when it contains horned or antlered members.

categories.prompt: Name an animal that can produce its own light.
categories.scope: Bioluminescence, including light produced by symbiotic bacteria in an animal's light organ, counts. Reflection, fluorescence and bright coloring alone do not. Broad animal groups count when they contain documented luminous members.

categories.prompt: Name an animal that makes a regular seasonal migration.
categories.scope: Named species and animal groups with documented recurring seasonal, breeding or feeding migrations count, including migrating populations of a species. One-off escapes or an individual simply wandering do not.

categories.prompt: Name a food crop with an edible part that normally grows underground.
categories.scope: Roots, tubers, rhizomes, bulbs, corms and underground fruits count. Named crop kinds and established edible varieties count. A normal above-ground fruit does not count merely because the plant has roots.

categories.prompt: Name a bone or named group of bones in the human skeleton.
categories.scope: Standard named bones, fused bones and familiar bone groups count. Left and right instances are the same answer. Cartilage, joints, muscles and organs are not bones.

categories.prompt: Name a unit used to measure a physical quantity or digital information.
categories.scope: Established metric, customary, historical and scientific measurement units count, including named prefixed units. Currency units and arbitrary made-up units do not. Official unit symbols are accepted only when they name that actual unit.

categories.prompt: Name a structure or component found in a living cell.
categories.scope: Plant, animal, fungal and prokaryotic cell structures count. Whole organs or tissues are not structures inside one cell. Established molecular structures such as DNA and chromosomes count. Cellular structures and molecular assemblies count; an individual pigment such as chlorophyll is not an organelle or cell structure by itself.

categories.prompt: Name a playable hero in Overwatch.
categories.scope: The full official Overwatch roster in the October 25, 2026 snapshot counts, including heroes introduced while it was called Overwatch 2. Skins and unplayable story characters do not.

categories.prompt: Name a playable fighter in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.
categories.scope: All base-game, Echo and DLC fighters count. Pokémon Trainer's three Pokémon, the three Mii fighting styles, and Pyra/Mythra count separately. Alternate costumes share the original fighter's answer; Assist Trophies do not count.

categories.prompt: Name a Legendary or Mythical Pokémon.
categories.scope: Species classified as Legendary or Mythical in the pinned PokéAPI data count. Forms share their species' answer identity. Pseudo-Legendary is a fan label and does not make a species Legendary.

categories.prompt: Name a character from the Harry Potter books or films.
categories.scope: Identifiable characters in the Harry Potter novels, films and their epilogues count, including creatures, ghosts and portraits. Real actors are not their fictional characters. Same-name characters share one answer identity.

categories.prompt: Name a real mountain range.
categories.scope: Named ranges, chains, mountain systems and subranges count, anywhere in the world. A single peak by itself is not a range.

categories.prompt: Name a real museum.
categories.scope: Named museums and museum complexes count, including historical institutions. Multiple institutions with the same name share an answer identity. A type of museum or a fictional museum is not a named real institution.

categories.prompt: Name a type of cookie or biscuit, including named branded varieties.
categories.scope: Named cookie and sweet biscuit varieties, brands and traditional preparations count. Regional names for the same biscuit share one answer; a cake or cracker is not automatically a cookie.

categories.prompt: Name a pie, tart or flan.
categories.scope: Named sweet and savory pies, tarts and flans count. Established dishes conventionally called pies count even when they use mash, crumbs or cake, including Boston cream pie and whoopie pie. An ordinary cake without a conventional pie name, pizza or an uncrusted omelette does not qualify.

categories.prompt: Name a real ice-cream flavor.
categories.scope: Established ice-cream and gelato flavor names, including named branded flavors and dairy-free ice-cream equivalents, count. An invented combination is not automatically an established flavor. A sorbet-only flavor is not evidence of an ice-cream flavor.

categories.prompt: Name a breakfast cereal, cereal brand or named cereal product.
categories.scope: Named breakfast-cereal kinds, brands and products count, including hot cereals, muesli, granola and historical products. An unrelated food does not count just because its maker also sells cereal.

categories.prompt: Name a salad dressing.

categories.scope: People who actually served as U.S. president count once per person, including presidents who served nonconsecutive terms. Candidates, vice presidents and founding figures who never held the presidency do not.

categories.prompt: Name an ancient civilization or ancient people.
categories.scope: Documented ancient or premodern civilizations, archaeological cultures and peoples count. Mythical places and fictional civilizations do not.

categories.prompt: Name a real war or recognized armed conflict.
categories.scope: Named examples of the whole subject count, including documented historical examples. Real public synonyms share one answer; arbitrary initials and invented combinations do not.

categories.prompt: Name a car model, past or present.
categories.scope: Real production, low-volume and officially named concept passenger-car, SUV and pickup models count. Manufacturer names alone are not model names. Recognized public model names without the make are supported only where explicitly listed.

categories.prompt: Name a real statue, sculpture or public monument.
categories.scope: Documented named sculptures, statues and public commemorative monuments count. A fictional statue and an ordinary building without landmark or monument identity do not.
